title: EU Cyber Resilience Act -- Actively-Exploited Vulnerability Reporting (Sept 2026)
context: 2026-08-14 engine cycle -- Cyber Resilience Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847) actively-exploited-vulnerability reporting duties begin 11 September 2026; products with digital elements, including AI-enabled components, are in scope
body: The EU Cyber Resilience Act is the first horizontal product-security law that reaches AI-enabled products by way of the digital elements they contain. The clock that matters most right now is 11 September 2026: from that date, a manufacturer that becomes aware of an actively exploited vulnerability in a product with digital elements must notify ENISA and its coordinating CSIRT within 24 hours, and must inform users without undue delay. The answer-first lesson for an AI operator is that incident evidence is now a compliance asset, not a post-mortem. A signed, timestamped incident register that names the affected component, the containment action taken, and the measurement evidence attached satisfies the reporting duty with a record an auditor can re-verify against a published public key. The Council of AI frames the reporting obligation in the same boundary language it applies everywhere else: a product-security program can honestly claim monitored containment of known, actively exploited vulnerabilities -- it cannot honestly claim provable isolation from every future exploit. The verified measurement credential is what turns that honest boundary into auditable evidence: what was measured, when, and under what signature. Operators who arrive at the September deadline already carrying a signed incident index and per-axis measurement evidence are positioned to treat the 24-hour report as a mechanical publish step instead of a scramble.
